newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO says Israel still has to issue entry permits.
newsitem.headline: PLO says Israel still has to issue entry permits.

text.p: PLO officials said on Saturday Israel had yet to issue tens of thousands of promised entry permits for Palestinian workers.

The Israeli Defence Ministry announced on Thursday that beginning on Sunday it would permit 35,000 Palestinian workers to enter Israel and cancel all internal closures on the West Bank except that in force on Nablus.
Said al-Mudalla, director of employment at the Palestinian Ministry of Labour, asked if 35,000 workers would actually be able to enter Israel on Sunday, told Reuters:

"Absolutely not...Within the last couple of days we received about 4,400 permits for only the Gaza Strip, none for the West Bank. We expect between 3,000 to 3,500 workers to leave tomorrow for Israel."

Sixty thousand Palestinians from the West Bank and the Gaza Strip worked in Israel before Moslem suicide bombings in February and March prompted Israel to stop most of them from coming in. The closure was then gradually eased.

About 23,000 Palestinians worked in Israel before clashes last month spurred by Israeli policies in Jerusalem in which 60 Arabs and 15 Jews were killed. The fighting led to an Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip and West Bank cities.

The Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) which signed a 1993 interim peace deal with Israel that set up self-rule enclaves in most of the Gaza Strip and parts of the West Bank condemns the closure as collective punishment.
